arguments.content:
---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API: send and update messages, reply in threads, create channels, list channels and users, fetch conversation history, upload files, react to messages, and build Block Kit messages. Use when Gemini CLI needs to perform Slack operations with a bot or user token, such as posting notifications, querying workspace data, or automating Slack workflows.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Operate on a Slack workspace through the Web API. Send all requests through `scripts/slack_api.cjs`, which handles authentication, JSON payloads, cursor pagination, retries on rate limits and server errors, and truncates large responses so output stays concise.

Requires Node.js and a Slack token: pass `--token TOKEN` or set the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable.

## Quick Start

Call a method by name with JSON arguments:

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs auth.test
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Deploy complete"}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel"}' --paginate
```

Output is JSON on stdout. API errors go to stderr with a remediation hint (exit code 1); usage errors exit with code 2.

Useful flags: `--paginate` (follow cursor pagination), `--max-items N` (truncate long arrays; default 50), `--max-pages N` (page cap; default 10), `--token TOKEN`, `--url URL` (test overrides).

## Core Workflows

### Send messages

1. Resolve the channel ID with `conversations.list` or `conversations.info` — Slack addresses channels by ID (`C...`), not by name.
2. Post with `chat.postMessage`, using `text` for plain messages or `blocks` for rich messages (see references/block-kit.md).
3. Reply in a thread by passing the parent message's `ts` as `thread_ts`.
4. Update or delete with `chat.update` / `chat.delete` using the `ts` returned by the original post.

### Read workspace data

- `conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim"}' --paginate` — all channels and DMs
- `conversations.history '{"channel":"C123456","limit":100}'` — recent messages in a channel
- `conversations.replies '{"channel":"C123456","ts":"1700000000.123456"}'` — thread replies
- `users.list '{}' --paginate` — all workspace users
- `users.lookupByEmail '{"email":"person@example.com"}'` — find a user by email
- `search.messages '{"query":"from:@alice in:#general after:2024-01-01"}'` — search messages

### Manage channels

- `conversations.create '{"name":"project-x","is_private":false}'` — new channel
- `conversations.invite '{"channel":"C123456","users":["U111","U222"]}'` — invite members
- `conversations.open '{"users":"U111,U222"}'` — open a DM and get its channel ID
- `conversations.rename`, `conversations.setTopic`, `conversations.setPurpose`, `conversations.archive`

### React, upload, schedule

- `reactions.add '{"channel":"C123456","name":"white_check_mark","timestamp":"1700000000.123456"}'` — note the param is `timestamp` (the message `ts`)
- `files.upload '{"channels":"C123456","content":"report text","filename":"report.txt","title":"Weekly report"}'` — text uploads; binary uploads need multipart (see references/api.md)
- `chat.scheduleMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Reminder","post_at":1735689600}'` — post at a unix timestamp

## Authentication and Scopes

- Bot token (`xoxb-`) for app actions; user token (`xoxp-`) for user-scoped actions.
- The script sends the token as `Authorization: Bearer`.
- Each method requires specific OAuth scopes — check references/api.md. On `missing_scope`, add the scope to the Slack app and reinstall it.
- Verify a token with `auth.test` before debugging other failures.

## When to Read the References

- **references/api.md** — full endpoint catalog with required scopes, key parameters, pagination, rate limits, and gotchas. Read it when unsure about a method's parameters or scopes, or when a call fails.
- **references/block-kit.md** — JSON structure for rich messages and modals. Read it when composing messages with buttons, headers, fields, or images.

# Slack Web API Reference

Table of contents:
- [Authentication and Tokens](#authentication-and-tokens)
- [Conventions](#conventions)
- [Endpoint Catalog](#endpoint-catalog)
  - [Messages](#messages)
  - [Threads](#threads)
  - [Conversations (channels and DMs)](#conversations-channels-and-dms)
  - [Users](#users)
  - [Reactions and Pins](#reactions-and-pins)
  - [Files](#files)
  - [Search](#search)
  - [Team and Usergroups](#team-and-usergroups)
  - [Views (modals and home tabs)](#views-modals-and-home-tabs)
  - [Utility](#utility)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Rate Limits](#rate-limits)
- [Common Errors](#common-errors)
- [Gotchas](#gotchas)

All examples assume the helper script at `scripts/slack_api.cjs` and a token in `$SLACK_TOKEN`.

## Authentication and Tokens

- **Bot token (`xoxb-`)**: acts as the Slack app; use for most automation (posting messages, reading channels the bot is in).
- **User token (`xoxp-`)**: acts as a user; required for user-scoped endpoints (e.g., `users.setPresence`, `team.billing.info`).
- **App-level token (`xapp-`)**: for Socket Mode and Events API; must be sent via the `Authorization` header (the helper does this) — never as a `token` parameter.
- The helper always sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Tokens are scoped to one workspace (or org install) and carry OAuth scopes. `auth.test` verifies a token and returns its user/team.
- On `missing_scope`: add the scope in the Slack app settings, reinstall the app to the workspace, and use the new token.

## Conventions

- **IDs, not names**: channels are `C...`, users `U...`, DMs `D...`, groups `G...`, bots `B...`. Most methods reject names.
- **`ts` values are strings** like `"1700000000.123456"`. Reuse them as `thread_ts` (replies) or `timestamp` (reactions).
- **mrkdwn**: `text` is parsed as Slack markup by default (`*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<@U123>`, `<#C123>`, `<https://example.com|label>`). Pass `"mrkdwn": false` for plain text, `"link_names": true` to linkify `@name` and `#channel`.
- **JSON args**: pass arrays as JSON arrays, e.g. `"users":["U111","U222"]`.
- **`text` vs `blocks`**: when `blocks` is present it renders in-app; `text` is the fallback shown in notifications and accessibility tools. Provide both when practical.
- **Cursor pagination**: responses include `response_metadata.next_cursor`; pass it back as `cursor`. The helper's `--paginate` flag does this automatically.

## Endpoint Catalog

### Messages

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat.postMessage` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `text` or `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `link_names`, `mrkdwn`, `unfurl_links`, `parse` | Returns `ts` and `channel`; the core method |
| `chat.postEphemeral` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `user`, `text` | Message visible only to that user |
| `chat.update` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `ts`, `text` or `blocks` | Edit a message |
| `chat.delete` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `ts` | Delete a message |
| `chat.getPermalink` | none | `channel`, `message_ts` | Returns `permalink` |
| `chat.scheduleMessage` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `text`, `post_at` (unix seconds) | Returns `scheduled_message_id` |

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Hello <@U111>!","link_names":true}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.scheduleMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Standup reminder","post_at":1735689600}'
```

### Threads

- Reply to a thread with `chat.postMessage` and `"thread_ts":"<parent ts>"`.
- Read replies with `conversations.replies` (`channels:history`): `{"channel":"C...","ts":"<parent ts>"}`.
- Broadcast a reply to the whole channel with `"reply_broadcast": true`.

### Conversations (channels and DMs)

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `conversations.list` | `channels:read` | `types` (`public_channel,private_channel,mpim,im`), `limit`, `cursor`, `exclude_archived`, `team_id` | Paginated; use `--paginate` |
| `conversations.info` | `channels:read` | `channel`, `include_num_members` | |
| `conversations.history` | `channels:history` | `channel`, `limit` (max 999), `latest`, `oldest`, `inclusive` | Returns `messages`, `has_more` |
| `conversations.replies` | `channels:history` | `channel`, `ts` | Thread messages |
| `conversations.members` | `channels:read` | `channel`, `limit`, `cursor` | Member IDs |
| `conversations.create` | `channels:manage` | `name`, `is_private` | Returns the new channel ID |
| `conversations.invite` | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `users` (array) | |
| `conversations.kick` | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `user` | |
| `conversations.leave` | `channels:manage` | `channel` | |
| `conversations.archive` / `conversations.unarchive` | `channels:manage` | `channel` | |
| `conversations.rename` | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `name` | |
| `conversations.setTopic` / `conversations.setPurpose` | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `topic` / `purpose` | |
| `conversations.open` | `channels:manage` | `users` (comma-separated) or `channel` | Opens/returns a DM channel ID |
| `conversations.close` | `channels:manage` | `channel` | |

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel"}' --paginate
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.open '{"users":"U111,U222"}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.history '{"channel":"C123456","limit":50}'
```

Note: `conversations.*` supersedes the legacy `channels.*`, `groups.*`, `im.*`, and `mpim.*` methods.

### Users

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `users.list` | `users:read` | `limit`, `cursor` | Paginated; includes `deleted` flag |
| `users.info` | `users:read` | `user` | |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | `users:read.email` | `email` | |
| `users.getPresence` | `users:read` | `user` | `presence`: `active`/`away` |
| `users.setPresence` | `users:write` | `presence` (`auto`/`away`) | User token |
| `users.profile.get` / `users.profile.set` | `users.profile:read` / `users.profile:write` | `user`, `profile` (object) | Status text/emoji live in `profile.status_text` / `profile.status_emoji` |

### Reactions and Pins

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reactions.add` | `reactions:write` | `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), `timestamp` | `timestamp` is the message `ts` |
| `reactions.remove` | `reactions:write` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` | |
| `reactions.get` | `reactions:read` | `channel`, `timestamp` | Returns all reactions on a message |
| `pins.add` | `pins:write` | `channel`, `timestamp` | |
| `pins.list` | `pins:read` | `channel` | |

### Files

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `files.upload` | `files:write` | `channels` (comma-separated IDs), `content` (text) or `file` (binary), `filename`, `title`, `thread_ts`, `initial_comment` | The helper sends JSON, so binary uploads (`file` param) need multipart/form-data instead — use the Slack SDK or `curl` for those; use `content` for text |
| `files.info` | `files:read` | `file` | |
| `files.list` | `files:read` | `channel`, `ts_from`, `ts_to`, `limit` | |

### Search

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search.messages` | `search:read` | `query` | Query syntax: `from:@user`, `in:#channel`, `after:2024-01-01`, `before:...`, `has::emoji`, quoted phrases |
| `search.files` | `search:read` | `query` | |

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs search.messages '{"query":"from:@alice in:#general after:2024-01-01","count":50}'
```

### Team and Usergroups

| Method | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `team.info` | `team:read` | Workspace name, domain, icon |
| `team.billing.info` | `team:read` | Requires a user token |
| `usergroups.list` | `usergroups:read` | `include_users: true` to expand members |

### Views (modals and home tabs)

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `views.open` | `views:write` | `trigger_id`, `view` | `trigger_id` comes from an interactive payload or shortcut (Events API) |
| `views.push` | `views:write` | `trigger_id`, `view` | Pushes onto a modal stack |
| `views.update` | `views:write` | `view_id` or `external_id`, `view` | |
| `views.publish` | `views:write` | `user_id`, `view` | Sets the App Home tab |

See references/block-kit.md for `view` JSON (modals use `type: "modal"` with `title`, `blocks`, `submit`).

### Utility

- `auth.test` — no scope; returns token identity (`user_id`, `team_id`). Run this first when debugging.
- `api.test` — no scope; connectivity check.

## Pagination

- List endpoints paginate with `limit` + `cursor`; the next cursor is in `response_metadata.next_cursor`.
- Use `--paginate`; the helper merges pages (arrays are concatenated, scalars last-wins) and caps at `--max-pages` (default 10).
- Typical max `limit` values: `conversations.list` 200, `users.list` 200, `conversations.history` 999, `search.messages` 100.

## Rate Limits

- Slack rate limits are per-method tiers (roughly: search tier 1, most reads tier 3, `chat.postMessage` tier 4 — tens to hundreds of requests per minute).
- Exceeding a tier returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header. The helper retries automatically (3 attempts) and respects `Retry-After`.
- For bulk operations, add small sleeps between calls and batch reads into single paginated calls rather than many small ones.

## Common Errors

| error | meaning | fix |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_auth` | Bad token | Check `--token` / `$SLACK_TOKEN`; run `auth.test` |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks required scope | Add scope in Slack app, reinstall |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot/user not in channel | `conversations.invite` first |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad channel ID or name used | Use the `C...` ID from `conversations.list` |
| `is_archived` | Channel archived | `conversations.unarchive` |
| `rate_limited` | 429 hit | Wait; helper retries automatically |
| `invalid_arguments` | Bad parameter | Re-check params against this reference |
| `internal_error` | Slack-side failure | Retry |

## Gotchas

- Address channels and users by ID, never by display name.
- `reactions.add` uses `timestamp`, not `ts`, for the message identifier.
- In `conversations.history`, parents of threads appear with `reply_count`; get the actual thread with `conversations.replies`.
- Bot-posted messages cannot be edited/deleted with a different user token; use the same bot token.
- `as_user` is deprecated — bot tokens always post as the bot.
- Deleting channels requires the admin API (`admin.conversations.delete`) with an admin user token; regular tokens cannot delete channels.
- When `blocks` are present, `text` still matters: it is used in notifications and for accessibility.

# Block Kit Reference

Table of contents:
- [Basics](#basics)
- [Text Objects](#text-objects)
- [Blocks](#blocks)
  - [header](#header)
  - [section](#section)
  - [divider](#divider)
  - [context](#context)
  - [actions](#actions)
  - [input](#input)
  - [image](#image)
- [Interactivity](#interactivity)
- [Example: Announcement Card](#example-announcement-card)
- [Example: Data Card with Fields](#example-data-card-with-fields)
- [Example: Modal](#example-modal)
- [Limits](#limits)

## Basics

- A Block Kit message is a JSON array of blocks passed as `blocks` to `chat.postMessage` / `chat.update`, or as `view.blocks` in `views.open` / `views.publish`.
- Keep `text` alongside `blocks`: it is the fallback shown in notifications.
- Max 50 blocks per message. See [Limits](#limits) for per-block text caps.
- Post with the helper:

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Fallback text","blocks":[ ... ]}'
```

## Text Objects

Two types: `mrkdwn` (rich) and `plain_text` (literal).

```json
{ "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Bold* and <@U111> and <https://example.com|link>" }
{ "type": "plain_text", "text": "Literal text", "emoji": true }
```

mrkdwn supports `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, mentions `<@U123>`, channel refs `<#C123>`, and links `<https://url|label>`.

## Blocks

### header

```json
{ "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Deploy Complete" } }
```

Max 150 characters.

### section

The workhorse block: `text`, optional `fields` (up to 10), optional `accessory`.

```json
{
  "type": "section",
  "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Build #42 passed in 3m 12s." },
  "fields": [
    { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Environment:*\nproduction" },
    { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Triggered by:*\n<@U111>" }
  ],
  "accessory": {
    "type": "button",
    "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "View logs" },
    "action_id": "view_logs",
    "url": "https://ci.example.com/builds/42"
  }
}
```

### divider

```json
{ "type": "divider" }
```

### context

Small text/images below the main content.

```json
{
  "type": "context",
  "elements": [
    { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Posted by <@U111>" },
    { "type": "image", "image_url": "https://example.com/icon.png", "alt_text": "icon" }
  ]
}
```

### actions

A row of interactive elements (buttons, selects, overflow menus).

```json
{
  "type": "actions",
  "elements": [
    {
      "type": "button",
      "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Approve" },
      "action_id": "approve_request",
      "value": "req-42",
      "style": "primary"
    },
    {
      "type": "button",
      "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Reject" },
      "action_id": "reject_request",
      "value": "req-42",
      "style": "danger"
    }
  ]
}
```

### input

Only valid inside modals (`views.open` / `views.push` / `views.update`), not in channel messages.

```json
{
  "type": "input",
  "block_id": "title",
  "label": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Title" },
  "element": { "type": "plain_text_input", "action_id": "title_input" },
  "optional": false
}
```

Other element types: `static_select`, `external_select`, `multi_static_select`, `datepicker`, `checkboxes`, `radio_buttons`.

### image

```json
{
  "type": "image",
  "image_url": "https://example.com/chart.png",
  "alt_text": "Monthly chart",
  "title": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Usage" }
}
```

## Interactivity

- `action_id` (max 255 chars) identifies which element was clicked; `value` (max 2000 chars) carries opaque data back to your app; `style` is `primary` or `danger`.
- Buttons with `url` open a browser link instead of firing a payload.
- Click events are delivered through the Events API, not the Web API — configure a request URL / Socket Mode in the Slack app for your app to receive them. This skill covers the Web API side: building and posting the blocks.

## Example: Announcement Card

```json
{
  "channel": "C123456",
  "text": "New policy published",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "New Policy Published" } },
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": {
        "type": "mrkdwn",
        "text": "The updated *remote work policy* is now in effect. Key changes:\n- Flexible hours expanded\n- New equipment stipend\n\nSee <https://wiki.example.com/policy|the full policy>."
      }
    },
    { "type": "context", "elements": [{ "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "By <@U111> · #announcements" }] }
  ]
}
```

## Example: Data Card with Fields

```json
{
  "channel": "C123456",
  "text": "Daily metrics",
  "blocks": [
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Daily metrics — 2024-01-15*" },
      "fields": [
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Active users:*\n1,204" },
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*New signups:*\n87" },
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Conversion:*\n7.2%" },
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Incidents:*\n0" }
      ]
    },
    { "type": "divider" },
    {
      "type": "actions",
      "elements": [
        {
          "type": "button",
          "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Open dashboard" },
          "action_id": "open_dashboard",
          "url": "https://metrics.example.com"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Example: Modal

Modals require a `trigger_id`, obtained from a shortcut or interactive payload (Events API), and a view with `type: "modal"`.

```json
{
  "trigger_id": "TRIGGER_ID_HERE",
  "view": {
    "type": "modal",
    "title": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Create Ticket" },
    "submit": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Submit" },
    "close": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Cancel" },
    "blocks": [
      {
        "type": "input",
        "block_id": "summary",
        "label": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Summary" },
        "element": { "type": "plain_text_input", "action_id": "summary_input" }
      },
      {
        "type": "input",
        "block_id": "priority",
        "label": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Priority" },
        "element": {
          "type": "static_select",
          "action_id": "priority_select",
          "options": [
            { "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Low" }, "value": "low" },
            { "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "High" }, "value": "high" }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs views.open '{"trigger_id":"...","view":{...}}'
```

## Limits

| Item | Limit |
|---|---|
| Blocks per message / view | 50 |
| `section` text | 3,000 chars |
| `section` fields | 10 |
| `context` elements | 10 |
| `header` text | 150 chars |
| `button` label | 75 chars |
| `action_id` | 255 chars |
| `value` (button) | 2,000 chars |
| `input` label | 2,000 chars |

arguments.content:
---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API: send and update messages, reply in threads, create channels, list channels and users, fetch conversation history, upload files, react to messages, and build Block Kit messages. Use when Gemini CLI needs to perform Slack operations with a bot or user token, such as posting notifications, querying workspace data, or automating Slack workflows.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Operate on a Slack workspace through the Web API. Send all requests through `scripts/slack_api.cjs`, which handles authentication, JSON payloads, cursor pagination, retries on rate limits and server errors, and truncates large responses so output stays concise.

Requires Node.js and a Slack token: pass `--token TOKEN` or set the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable.

## Quick Start

Call a method by name with JSON arguments:

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs auth.test
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Deploy complete"}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel"}' --paginate
```

Output is JSON on stdout. API errors go to stderr with a remediation hint (exit code 1); usage errors exit with code 2.

Useful flags: `--paginate` (follow cursor pagination), `--max-items N` (truncate long arrays; default 50), `--max-pages N` (page cap; default 10), `--token TOKEN`, `--url URL` (test overrides).

## Core Workflows

### Send messages

1. Resolve the channel ID with `conversations.list` or `conversations.info` — Slack addresses channels by ID (`C...`), not by name.
2. Post with `chat.postMessage`, using `text` for plain messages or `blocks` for rich messages (see references/block-kit.md).
3. Reply in a thread by passing the parent message's `ts` as `thread_ts`.
4. Update or delete with `chat.update` / `chat.delete` using the `ts` returned by the original post.

### Read workspace data

- `conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim"}' --paginate` — all channels and DMs
- `conversations.history '{"channel":"C123456","limit":100}'` — recent messages in a channel
- `conversations.replies '{"channel":"C123456","ts":"1700000000.123456"}'` — thread replies
- `users.list '{}' --paginate` — all workspace users
- `users.lookupByEmail '{"email":"person@example.com"}'` — find a user by email
- `search.messages '{"query":"from:@alice in:#general after:2024-01-01"}'` — search messages

### Manage channels

- `conversations.create '{"name":"project-x","is_private":false}'` — new channel
- `conversations.invite '{"channel":"C123456","users":["U111","U222"]}'` — invite members
- `conversations.open '{"users":"U111,U222"}'` — open a DM and get its channel ID
- `conversations.rename`, `conversations.setTopic`, `conversations.setPurpose`, `conversations.archive`

### React, upload, schedule

- `reactions.add '{"channel":"C123456","name":"white_check_mark","timestamp":"1700000000.123456"}'` — note the param is `timestamp` (the message `ts`)
- `files.upload '{"channels":"C123456","content":"report text","filename":"report.txt","title":"Weekly report"}'` — text uploads; binary uploads need multipart (see references/api.md)
- `chat.scheduleMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Reminder","post_at":1735689600}'` — post at a unix timestamp

## Authentication and Scopes

- Bot token (`xoxb-`) for app actions; user token (`xoxp-`) for user-scoped actions.
- The script sends the token as `Authorization: Bearer`.
- Each method requires specific OAuth scopes — check references/api.md. On `missing_scope`, add the scope to the Slack app and reinstall it.
- Verify a token with `auth.test` before debugging other failures.

## When to Read the References

- **references/api.md** — full endpoint catalog with required scopes, key parameters, pagination, rate limits, and gotchas. Read it when unsure about a method's parameters or scopes, or when a call fails.
- **references/block-kit.md** — JSON structure for rich messages and modals. Read it when composing messages with buttons, headers, fields, or images.

# Slack Web API Reference

Table of contents:
- [Authentication and Tokens](#authentication-and-tokens)
- [Conventions](#conventions)
- [Endpoint Catalog](#endpoint-catalog)
  - [Messages](#messages)
  - [Threads](#threads)
  - [Conversations (channels and DMs)](#conversations-channels-and-dms)
  - [Users](#users)
  - [Reactions and Pins](#reactions-and-pins)
  - [Files](#files)
  - [Search](#search)
  - [Team and Usergroups](#team-and-usergroups)
  - [Views (modals and home tabs)](#views-modals-and-home-tabs)
  - [Utility](#utility)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Rate Limits](#rate-limits)
- [Common Errors](#common-errors)
- [Gotchas](#gotchas)

All examples assume the helper script at `scripts/slack_api.cjs` and a token in `$SLACK_TOKEN`.

## Authentication and Tokens

- **Bot token (`xoxb-`)**: acts as the Slack app; use for most automation (posting messages, reading channels the bot is in).
- **User token (`xoxp-`)**: acts as a user; required for user-scoped endpoints (e.g., `users.setPresence`, `team.billing.info`).
- **App-level token (`xapp-`)**: for Socket Mode and Events API; must be sent via the `Authorization` header (the helper does this) — never as a `token` parameter.
- The helper always sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Tokens are scoped to one workspace (or org install) and carry OAuth scopes. `auth.test` verifies a token and returns its user/team.
- On `missing_scope`: add the scope in the Slack app settings, reinstall the app to the workspace, and use the new token.

## Conventions

- **IDs, not names**: channels are `C...`, users `U...`, DMs `D...`, groups `G...`, bots `B...`. Most methods reject names.
- **`ts` values are strings** like `"1700000000.123456"`. Reuse them as `thread_ts` (replies) or `timestamp` (reactions).
- **mrkdwn**: `text` is parsed as Slack markup by default (`*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<@U123>`, `<#C123>`, `<https://example.com|label>`). Pass `"mrkdwn": false` for plain text, `"link_names": true` to linkify `@name` and `#channel`.
- **JSON args**: pass arrays as JSON arrays, e.g. `"users":["U111","U222"]`.
- **`text` vs `blocks`**: when `blocks` is present it renders in-app; `text` is the fallback shown in notifications and accessibility tools. Provide both when practical.
- **Cursor pagination**: responses include `response_metadata.next_cursor`; pass it back as `cursor`. The helper's `--paginate` flag does this automatically.

## Endpoint Catalog

### Messages

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat.postMessage` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `text` or `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `link_names`, `mrkdwn`, `unfurl_links`, `parse` | Returns `ts` and `channel`; the core method |
| `chat.postEphemeral` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `user`, `text` | Message visible only to that user |
| `chat.update` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `ts`, `text` or `blocks` | Edit a message |
| `chat.delete` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `ts` | Delete a message |
| `chat.getPermalink` | none | `channel`, `message_ts` | Returns `permalink` |
| `chat.scheduleMessage` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `text`, `post_at` (unix seconds) | Returns `scheduled_message_id` |

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Hello <@U111>!","link_names":true}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.scheduleMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Standup reminder","post_at":1735689600}'
```

### Threads

- Reply to a thread with `chat.postMessage` and `"thread_ts":"<parent ts>"`.
- Read replies with `conversations.replies` (`channels:history`): `{"channel":"C...","ts":"<parent ts>"}`.
- Broadcast a reply to the whole channel with `"reply_broadcast": true`.

### Conversations (channels and DMs)

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `conversations.list` | `channels:read` | `types` (`public_channel,private_channel,mpim,im`), `limit`, `cursor`, `exclude_archived`, `team_id` | Paginated; use `--paginate` |
| `conversations.info` | `channels:read` | `channel`, `include_num_members` | |
| `conversations.history` | `channels:history` | `channel`, `limit` (max 999), `latest`, `oldest`, `inclusive` | Returns `messages`, `has_more` |
| `conversations.replies` | `channels:history` | `channel`, `ts` | Thread messages |
| `conversations.members` | `channels:read` | `channel`, `limit`, `cursor` | Member IDs |
| `conversations.create` | `channels:manage` | `name`, `is_private` | Returns the new channel ID |
| `conversations.invite` | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `users` (array) | |
| `conversations.kick` | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `user` | |
| `conversations.leave` | `channels:manage` | `channel` | |
| `conversations.archive` / `conversations.unarchive` | `channels:manage` | `channel` | |
| `conversations.rename` | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `name` | |
| `conversations.setTopic` / `conversations.setPurpose` | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `topic` / `purpose` | |
| `conversations.open` | `channels:manage` | `users` (comma-separated) or `channel` | Opens/returns a DM channel ID |
| `conversations.close` | `channels:manage` | `channel` | |

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel"}' --paginate
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.open '{"users":"U111,U222"}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.history '{"channel":"C123456","limit":50}'
```

Note: `conversations.*` supersedes the legacy `channels.*`, `groups.*`, `im.*`, and `mpim.*` methods.

### Users

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `users.list` | `users:read` | `limit`, `cursor` | Paginated; includes `deleted` flag |
| `users.info` | `users:read` | `user` | |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | `users:read.email` | `email` | |
| `users.getPresence` | `users:read` | `user` | `presence`: `active`/`away` |
| `users.setPresence` | `users:write` | `presence` (`auto`/`away`) | User token |
| `users.profile.get` / `users.profile.set` | `users.profile:read` / `users.profile:write` | `user`, `profile` (object) | Status text/emoji live in `profile.status_text` / `profile.status_emoji` |

### Reactions and Pins

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reactions.add` | `reactions:write` | `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), `timestamp` | `timestamp` is the message `ts` |
| `reactions.remove` | `reactions:write` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` | |
| `reactions.get` | `reactions:read` | `channel`, `timestamp` | Returns all reactions on a message |
| `pins.add` | `pins:write` | `channel`, `timestamp` | |
| `pins.list` | `pins:read` | `channel` | |

### Files

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `files.upload` | `files:write` | `channels` (comma-separated IDs), `content` (text) or `file` (binary), `filename`, `title`, `thread_ts`, `initial_comment` | The helper sends JSON, so binary uploads (`file` param) need multipart/form-data instead — use the Slack SDK or `curl` for those; use `content` for text |
| `files.info` | `files:read` | `file` | |
| `files.list` | `files:read` | `channel`, `ts_from`, `ts_to`, `limit` | |

### Search

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search.messages` | `search:read` | `query` | Query syntax: `from:@user`, `in:#channel`, `after:2024-01-01`, `before:...`, `has::emoji`, quoted phrases |
| `search.files` | `search:read` | `query` | |

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs search.messages '{"query":"from:@alice in:#general after:2024-01-01","count":50}'
```

### Team and Usergroups

| Method | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `team.info` | `team:read` | Workspace name, domain, icon |
| `team.billing.info` | `team:read` | Requires a user token |
| `usergroups.list` | `usergroups:read` | `include_users: true` to expand members |

### Views (modals and home tabs)

| Method | Scope | Key params | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `views.open` | `views:write` | `trigger_id`, `view` | `trigger_id` comes from an interactive payload or shortcut (Events API) |
| `views.push` | `views:write` | `trigger_id`, `view` | Pushes onto a modal stack |
| `views.update` | `views:write` | `view_id` or `external_id`, `view` | |
| `views.publish` | `views:write` | `user_id`, `view` | Sets the App Home tab |

See references/block-kit.md for `view` JSON (modals use `type: "modal"` with `title`, `blocks`, `submit`).

### Utility

- `auth.test` — no scope; returns token identity (`user_id`, `team_id`). Run this first when debugging.
- `api.test` — no scope; connectivity check.

## Pagination

- List endpoints paginate with `limit` + `cursor`; the next cursor is in `response_metadata.next_cursor`.
- Use `--paginate`; the helper merges pages (arrays are concatenated, scalars last-wins) and caps at `--max-pages` (default 10).
- Typical max `limit` values: `conversations.list` 200, `users.list` 200, `conversations.history` 999, `search.messages` 100.

## Rate Limits

- Slack rate limits are per-method tiers (roughly: search tier 1, most reads tier 3, `chat.postMessage` tier 4 — tens to hundreds of requests per minute).
- Exceeding a tier returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header. The helper retries automatically (3 attempts) and respects `Retry-After`.
- For bulk operations, add small sleeps between calls and batch reads into single paginated calls rather than many small ones.

## Common Errors

| error | meaning | fix |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_auth` | Bad token | Check `--token` / `$SLACK_TOKEN`; run `auth.test` |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks required scope | Add scope in Slack app, reinstall |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot/user not in channel | `conversations.invite` first |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad channel ID or name used | Use the `C...` ID from `conversations.list` |
| `is_archived` | Channel archived | `conversations.unarchive` |
| `rate_limited` | 429 hit | Wait; helper retries automatically |
| `invalid_arguments` | Bad parameter | Re-check params against this reference |
| `internal_error` | Slack-side failure | Retry |

## Gotchas

- Address channels and users by ID, never by display name.
- `reactions.add` uses `timestamp`, not `ts`, for the message identifier.
- In `conversations.history`, parents of threads appear with `reply_count`; get the actual thread with `conversations.replies`.
- Bot-posted messages cannot be edited/deleted with a different user token; use the same bot token.
- `as_user` is deprecated — bot tokens always post as the bot.
- Deleting channels requires the admin API (`admin.conversations.delete`) with an admin user token; regular tokens cannot delete channels.
- When `blocks` are present, `text` still matters: it is used in notifications and for accessibility.

# Block Kit Reference

Table of contents:
- [Basics](#basics)
- [Text Objects](#text-objects)
- [Blocks](#blocks)
  - [header](#header)
  - [section](#section)
  - [divider](#divider)
  - [context](#context)
  - [actions](#actions)
  - [input](#input)
  - [image](#image)
- [Interactivity](#interactivity)
- [Example: Announcement Card](#example-announcement-card)
- [Example: Data Card with Fields](#example-data-card-with-fields)
- [Example: Modal](#example-modal)
- [Limits](#limits)

## Basics

- A Block Kit message is a JSON array of blocks passed as `blocks` to `chat.postMessage` / `chat.update`, or as `view.blocks` in `views.open` / `views.publish`.
- Keep `text` alongside `blocks`: it is the fallback shown in notifications.
- Max 50 blocks per message. See [Limits](#limits) for per-block text caps.
- Post with the helper:

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Fallback text","blocks":[ ... ]}'
```

## Text Objects

Two types: `mrkdwn` (rich) and `plain_text` (literal).

```json
{ "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Bold* and <@U111> and <https://example.com|link>" }
{ "type": "plain_text", "text": "Literal text", "emoji": true }
```

mrkdwn supports `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, mentions `<@U123>`, channel refs `<#C123>`, and links `<https://url|label>`.

## Blocks

### header

```json
{ "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Deploy Complete" } }
```

Max 150 characters.

### section

The workhorse block: `text`, optional `fields` (up to 10), optional `accessory`.

```json
{
  "type": "section",
  "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Build #42 passed in 3m 12s." },
  "fields": [
    { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Environment:*\nproduction" },
    { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Triggered by:*\n<@U111>" }
  ],
  "accessory": {
    "type": "button",
    "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "View logs" },
    "action_id": "view_logs",
    "url": "https://ci.example.com/builds/42"
  }
}
```

### divider

```json
{ "type": "divider" }
```

### context

Small text/images below the main content.

```json
{
  "type": "context",
  "elements": [
    { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Posted by <@U111>" },
    { "type": "image", "image_url": "https://example.com/icon.png", "alt_text": "icon" }
  ]
}
```

### actions

A row of interactive elements (buttons, selects, overflow menus).

```json
{
  "type": "actions",
  "elements": [
    {
      "type": "button",
      "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Approve" },
      "action_id": "approve_request",
      "value": "req-42",
      "style": "primary"
    },
    {
      "type": "button",
      "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Reject" },
      "action_id": "reject_request",
      "value": "req-42",
      "style": "danger"
    }
  ]
}
```

### input

Only valid inside modals (`views.open` / `views.push` / `views.update`), not in channel messages.

```json
{
  "type": "input",
  "block_id": "title",
  "label": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Title" },
  "element": { "type": "plain_text_input", "action_id": "title_input" },
  "optional": false
}
```

Other element types: `static_select`, `external_select`, `multi_static_select`, `datepicker`, `checkboxes`, `radio_buttons`.

### image

```json
{
  "type": "image",
  "image_url": "https://example.com/chart.png",
  "alt_text": "Monthly chart",
  "title": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Usage" }
}
```

## Interactivity

- `action_id` (max 255 chars) identifies which element was clicked; `value` (max 2000 chars) carries opaque data back to your app; `style` is `primary` or `danger`.
- Buttons with `url` open a browser link instead of firing a payload.
- Click events are delivered through the Events API, not the Web API — configure a request URL / Socket Mode in the Slack app for your app to receive them. This skill covers the Web API side: building and posting the blocks.

## Example: Announcement Card

```json
{
  "channel": "C123456",
  "text": "New policy published",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "New Policy Published" } },
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": {
        "type": "mrkdwn",
        "text": "The updated *remote work policy* is now in effect. Key changes:\n- Flexible hours expanded\n- New equipment stipend\n\nSee <https://wiki.example.com/policy|the full policy>."
      }
    },
    { "type": "context", "elements": [{ "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "By <@U111> · #announcements" }] }
  ]
}
```

## Example: Data Card with Fields

```json
{
  "channel": "C123456",
  "text": "Daily metrics",
  "blocks": [
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Daily metrics — 2024-01-15*" },
      "fields": [
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Active users:*\n1,204" },
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*New signups:*\n87" },
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Conversion:*\n7.2%" },
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Incidents:*\n0" }
      ]
    },
    { "type": "divider" },
    {
      "type": "actions",
      "elements": [
        {
          "type": "button",
          "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Open dashboard" },
          "action_id": "open_dashboard",
          "url": "https://metrics.example.com"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Example: Modal

Modals require a `trigger_id`, obtained from a shortcut or interactive payload (Events API), and a view with `type: "modal"`.

```json
{
  "trigger_id": "TRIGGER_ID_HERE",
  "view": {
    "type": "modal",
    "title": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Create Ticket" },
    "submit": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Submit" },
    "close": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Cancel" },
    "blocks": [
      {
        "type": "input",
        "block_id": "summary",
        "label": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Summary" },
        "element": { "type": "plain_text_input", "action_id": "summary_input" }
      },
      {
        "type": "input",
        "block_id": "priority",
        "label": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Priority" },
        "element": {
          "type": "static_select",
          "action_id": "priority_select",
          "options": [
            { "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Low" }, "value": "low" },
            { "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "High" }, "value": "high" }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```
node scripts/slack_api.cjs views.open '{"trigger_id":"...","view":{...}}'
```

## Limits

| Item | Limit |
|---|---|
| Blocks per message / view | 50 |
| `section` text | 3,000 chars |
| `section` fields | 10 |
| `context` elements | 10 |
| `header` text | 150 chars |
| `button` label | 75 chars |
| `action_id` | 255 chars |
| `value` (button) | 2,000 chars |
| `input` label | 2,000 chars |
